Yet India has surpassed its previous best of 111 medals there, when it finished fifth and bettered the 72-medal return from Jakarta in 2018, where 190 athletes represented the country.Track and field athletes were the standout, collecting 65 medals, including 22 gold. Para-badminton was next biggest contributor with 16, meaning the two events combined for 81 medals — more than 70 percent of India’s tally. The numbers underline how effectively a squad converted opportunity into podium finishes.Friday brought a flourish, with India winning nine gold medals — its best singleday gold haul of these Games. Sandeep stormed to the men’s 400m T64 title in a world-record 52.28s, while Haney won the men’s javelin F37/38 gold with a worldrecord throw of 60.49m.Sumit Antil, the Paralympic champion, defended his javelin crown in the men’s F42-44/61-64 combined event with a throw of 72.46m.It was not a record, but enough to lead an Indian sweep: Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar bronze with 64.48m.Pranav Soorma defended his men’s club throw F51 title with a Games-record 32.87m. Sandeep’s compatriot Ajay Kumar claimed bronze in 400m T64 in a Games-record 53.61s. Nimisha C won silver in women’s long jump T47 with 5.37m, while Parmod Bijarnia took silver in the men’s 1500m T46 in 4:09.65.India stood fourth on Friday, ahead of South Korea, which has 28 gold, 36 silver and 33 bronze (97). With finals scheduled for Saturday and no Indian entries in those events, the ranking remained vulnerable: three Korean gold would take them to 31 and move them ahead. Even two would level the gold count at 30, with Korea’s silver advantage deciding the tie-break.Whatever the final order, India’s record haul has made this a landmark campaign.

Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has added a new chapter to his illustrious sporting journey, this time away from the court, after being elected to the Real Madrid Board of Directors with an overwhelming majority of votes. The 22-time Grand Slam champion's appointment was ratified at the Spanish football club's Extraordinary General Assembly on Friday, with 99.5 per cent of the votes cast in his favour.A total of 1,713 votes were recorded, of which 1,704 supported Nadal's appointment, while four voted against and five abstained. The announcement was met with a standing ovation from the club's representatives, underlining the affection and respect the Spanish sporting icon commands among Real Madrid supporters.Nadal, who has been an honorary member of Real Madrid since 2011, described his new role as both an honour and a significant responsibility, expressing his desire to contribute to the continued success of one of the world's biggest sporting institutions.Real Madrid president Florentino Perez welcomed Nadal's induction into the board, describing the occasion as a special moment for the club. He also praised the tennis great's achievements, character and longstanding association with the Spanish giants."We all know the extraordinary stature of Rafa Nadal. His name is already part of the universal history of sport. He has achieved something that is within reach of very few: becoming a legend admired and respected in every corner of the world," Perez said, as quoted in the club's official statement.The Real Madrid president also highlighted Nadal's connection with the club, pointing to his passion for the team and his association with its values."Rafa is a person who has earned the respect and affection of millions of people because of his character, his behaviour on and off the courts, and his unwavering commitment to the values that make sport great. And for us there is something that has a very special meaning: Rafa is one of our own. He is an honorary member of Real Madrid, he feels deeply about these colours and has always proudly expressed his Madridismo," he added.Perez further expressed confidence that Nadal's presence would help the club maintain its identity and continue building for future generations.Responding to his appointment, Nadal said joining the Real Madrid Board of Directors was a moment of immense pride, while acknowledging the responsibility that came with representing a globally recognised sporting institution."It's a great responsibility to be part of the Real Madrid Board of Directors. This club is passed down from parents to children and unites people. For me, it unites me with my family and friends to watch the matches together. It's a great honour and a great source of satisfaction," Nadal said.The former world No. 1 also underlined his intention to contribute to the club's continued success, while expressing his understanding of the expectations attached to his new position."I am very aware of the responsibility because Real Madrid is a global brand. It is an immense responsibility, and I accept it so that over time I can learn and contribute to ensuring that this club remains the best in the world," he added.Nadal also reiterated his commitment to helping Real Madrid preserve its status as one of the most successful clubs in world football."I'm going to work to ensure things stay the way they are: a successful club, and that it continues to be so in the years to come. Hala Madrid," he said.
Article Summary: Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has been elected to the Real Madrid Board of Directors. Nadal's appointment was ratified at the Spanish football club's Extraordinary General Assembly on Friday, with 99.5 per cent of the votes cast in his favour. The 22-time Grand Slam champion has been an honorary member of Real Madrid since 2011.

Article Title: Premier League: 14 years, 20 defeats — Fulham finally end Man City's dominance with a draw

Muniz strikes before Anderson rescues a point

Manchester City's long-standing dominance over Fulham came to an end on Saturday as the two sides played out a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium, extending their winless run in the Premier League to four matches.The result ended Fulham's 20-match losing streak against City in all competitions, dating back to 2012, and brought an end to a remarkable 14-year run of defeats against the Manchester club.City avoided a fourth successive league defeat but once again delivered an unconvincing performance, dropping more points in the title race. They remain third in the standings, five points behind leaders Arsenal, who can extend their advantage with a win against Newcastle United later on Saturday.Fulham made a bright start and took the lead in the 16th minute through Rodrigo Muniz, who finished clinically after being set up by former City player Oscar Bobb.City thought they had equalised eight minutes later when Erling Haaland bundled the ball over the line after Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno had saved his initial close-range effort. However, VAR ruled out the goal, judging that Haaland had kicked the ball out of Leno's hands.The Premier League later explained that Leno was deemed to be "in control of the ball".Haaland had earlier wasted two good opportunities, underlining City's struggles in front of goal as Fulham defended resolutely.The hosts eventually found their breakthrough in the 57th minute when Elliott Anderson produced a superb volley from the edge of the area. His effort flew through a crowd of players and into the bottom corner, earning City a point and marking his first Premier League goal since joining from Nottingham Forest.Both sides had opportunities to snatch a winner. Muniz was denied by City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma , while Fulham continued to threaten on the counter-attack.The visitors, however, held on for a deserved point and a landmark result against their long-time tormentors.
Article Summary: Manchester City and Fulham played out a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium. Rodrigo Muniz gave Fulham the lead in the 16th minute after being set up by Oscar Bobb. Erling Haaland had a goal disallowed for kicking the ball out of Bernd Leno's hands. Elliott Anderson scored City's equaliser in the 57th minute.

Article Title: 'I'll be back fresh and ready': Harry Kane vows stronger comeback after serious ankle injury

How did Harry Kane suffer the ankle injury?

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is determined to turn his latest injury setback into an opportunity to come back stronger, insisting he will return refreshed and ready for the crucial phase of the season in 2027. The England captain suffered a serious ankle injury during Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne on Friday, with the club confirming that he will be sidelined for several months. Kane took to social media to address the setback, expressing his disappointment while underlining his determination to overcome the challenge. The 33-year-old sustained a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle, ruling him out of action for an extended period."The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury, but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!" Kane wrote.The Bayern forward also shared an encouraging message he received from former NFL player Julian Edelman, using it as motivation to deal with the difficult phase of his career."'Tough times don't last, tough people do' – my guy @Edelman11 told me this one!" Kane added.The England captain also thanked supporters for their messages and wishes following the injury, ending his post with the German phrase "Alles gut", which translates to "All good".Kane picked up the injury shortly after Bayern fell behind against Cologne when defender Joel Schmied's challenge caught his left ankle. The striker attempted to continue playing but was eventually forced off in the 20th minute, with Tom Bischof replacing him.Bayern later confirmed the extent of the injury, announcing that Kane had suffered a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle. The German champions also suffered another injury concern during the contest, with French winger Michael Olise sustaining a bruised forefoot. Olise did not return for the second half and was seen leaving the stadium on crutches.
Article Summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane will be sidelined for several months. England captain sustained a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle. Kane took to social media to express his disappointment at the setback. The 33-year- old also shared an encouraging message he received from former NFL player Julian Edelman.

England captain Harry Kane is set for an extended spell on the sidelines after sustaining a ligament injury in his left ankle during Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne on Friday.The 33-year-old suffered the injury following a challenge from Cologne defender Joel Schmied. The incident occurred as Schmied attempted to intercept a low delivery from Michael Olise, reaching the ball first before making contact with Kane 's left leg in his follow-through near the back post.Kane was left in considerable pain and remained on the ground for treatment. Although he managed to get back on his feet and briefly continued, the Bayern striker was eventually forced to leave the pitch, hobbling off with the assistance of two physiotherapists.Bayern subsequently confirmed the extent of the injury, with medical examinations revealing damage to the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle. The German champions also indicated that their leading forward would be unavailable for the next few months."Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich's Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich's medical department.The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months," the club said in a statement.The injury comes as a major setback for Bayern, given Kane's importance to the side since arriving from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023. The England international has been the club's standout attacking figure, registering 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances while helping them secure two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup.Kane has also enjoyed significant individual success, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or last month. His long-term future at the German club appeared settled after he signed a contract extension just two weeks ago, keeping him in Bavaria until June 2029.However, his latest injury will now force Bayern to cope without their prolific forward for the coming months.
Article Summary: England captain Harry Kane is set for an extended spell on the sidelines after sustaining a ligament injury in his left ankle. The 33-year-old suffered the injury during Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne on Friday. The incident occurred as Schmied attempted to intercept a low delivery from Michael Olise.
